messages:
sofia: quick check — hitting flaky auth 401s in Next Edge after bundling. TS SDK built as ESM; works locally but on Vercel Edge some requests 401 and some streaming responses fail mid-stream. anyone seen this?
kevin: what does "built as ESM" mean exactly? package.json has \"type\":\"module\" only or do you publish a CJS build too?
sofia: package.json has \"type\": \"module\" and we ship dist/index.mjs. importing in edge route like `import SDK from 'redwood-js-sdk'`. bundler is Vite/Next edge runtime.
anna: Vercel Edge is strict ESM and will not polyfill node built-ins. If the SDK pulls in node internals or a fetch shim, bundlers sometimes replace things weirdly which can drop headers.
kevin: can you paste how you construct the client / pass the key?
sofia: snippet:```\nconst client = new SDK({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });\nconst res = await client.streamCompletion({ prompt });\n```
kevin: FYI process.env is compiled at build time by Vite. Make sure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in Vercel env vars (Edge runtime reads env at build/runtime depending on config). If you rely on a runtime secret fetch it's async — that can confuse retry logic.
anna: also if the SDK auto-retries network errors, streaming responses are not re-playable. If a retry happens after the body is consumed you can get weird auth/no-auth races. For Edge, prefer synchronous auth retrieval.
ben: short workaround: pass header explicitly from the route:```\nawait fetch(url, {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type':'application/json' },\n  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })\n});\n```
sofia: ok will try that. curious why some requests succeed and others 401 though.
kevin: could be that some invocations use cached build-time env (undefined) while other ones use runtime env. Vite sometimes inlines `process.env` during build; make sure you're not bundling a default fallback.
anna: packaging note — publish dual entrypoints and conditional exports:```\n"exports": {\n  ".": {\n    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",\n    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"\n  }\n}\n```
and include a tiny CJS wrapper for older bundlers. That avoids ambiguous resolution in SSR/builds.
ben: streaming quirk: Vercel Edge fetch returns a Web ReadableStream; Node layers use Node streams. Make SDK agnostic or convert: use `response.body.getReader()` for browser/edge, and `response.body.on('data')` for Node. Also avoid consuming the stream inside SDK middleware if you want retries.
kevin: pragmatic fixes: 1) make streaming calls non-retryable by default, 2) require callers to pass `retry: true` for idempotent non-streaming ops, 3) ensure auth retrieval is sync for Edge.
sofia: how to detect streaming in the SDK?
anna: expose option like `{ stream: true, retry: false }` or check `res.headers.get('content-type')` for `text/event-stream`/`application/octet-stream`.
sofia: any Vite-specific gotchas to watch?
ben: Vite uses `import.meta.env` instead of `process.env`. If your code checks `process.env.NODE_ENV` it might be replaced weirdly. Avoid dynamic requires; use static imports or dynamic `import()` which Vite supports for ESM. Also watch for polyfills that inject a fake `process` object.
sofia: thanks — plan: 1) pass auth header explicitly from route, 2) disable auto-retry for stream calls, 3) add conditional exports to publishing pipeline, 4) test on canary. will report back with repro gist. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded with env var change :thumbsup:
sofia: thanks all, will follow up with a small repro gist if the 401s persist.
